title: OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility orchestrator: replayable snapshot + request/response shape translator
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: Customers calling Redwood with clients written for the OpenAI Chat Completions (CC) API expect identical request/response shapes, streaming chunk semantics, and deterministic function/tool calling behavior. We observe differences in: role/name field contractions, partial stream chunk boundaries for function calls, and non-deterministic toolcall attribution when we fall back to truncated model variants. This ticket implements an orchestrator that translates inbound OpenAI-CC requests into canonical Redwood runtime shapes, captures a replayable snapshot of request+prefix-state for deterministic replay (debugging/QA), and reconstitutes CC-compatible streaming and fn_call frames on the response path.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OA-CC requests are mapped to Redwood canonical request shape with a lossless transform for role/name/content and metadata
Streaming responses preserve chunk semantics expected by OA clients: function_call start/event/complete tokens are emitted across SSE/HTTP2 frames that mimic OpenAI ordering

Tool/function calling round-trip preserves 'name' attribution and arguments; when falling back to model variants the orchestrator emits compatibility warnings in telemetry but keeps cc-shaped responses
Snapshot feature captures prefix KV state, original request payload, and runtime routing decision; snapshots are small (<50KB typical) and stored for 7 days for replay
There is an automated replay harness in CI that can re-run 10 representative OA-CC transcripts and assert byte-identical post-translate streaming boundaries for both text and function call flows
End-to-end integration tests for streaming+tool-calls pass on Linux and macOS CI runners and are documented in the PR
Instrumentation emits events for mapping errors, dropped tokens, and fallback model usage to the console traces dashboard
No PII or secrets are persisted in snapshots; snapshot storage respects KMS policies for Private deployments
implementation_notes: Add a stateless 'translator' layer in the ingress path that performs: role/name normalization, message-level metadata mapping, and optional sanitization
Implement 'snapshot' as an opaque, gzipped JSON blob with explicit whitelist of fields (prompt, system messages, routing decision, KV prefix digest) and a TTL policy in the storage layer
Create a streaming re-emitter component that can coalesce Redwood token deltas into OA-compatible SSE frames; ensure each frame includes the same 'delta' ordering OA clients expect

Function call handling: detect early function_call initiation tokens in stream, buffer until 'complete' event or until a configurable chunk timeout, then emit a single 'function_call' complete event with preserved args

Fallback behavior: when choosing a quantized/compatible model variant, attach a deterministic 'compat_version' header in the response envelope and include a small compatibility hint in the telemetry event
Expose feature flag to opt-out of snapshotting per-customer for compliance-sensitive tenants
Favor idempotent transforms; maintain original request.id in translated payload to help crosswalk logs and traces
decisions: Snapshot TTL default: 7 days (can be overridden by enterprise contracts). Rationale: balances debugging usefulness vs storage costs
Use gzipped JSON for snapshot format to keep it portable between hosted and Private deployments
Do not attempt to canonicalize user-provided function schemas; preserve user payload exactly and add shim metadata instead
Emit compatibility header instead of mutating client-visible fields when falling back to model variants to avoid surprising clients

progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Spike complete — prototype translator normalizes 'assistant'/'system' role variants and canonicalizes function_call envelope. Found edge-case where some clients provide 'assistant.name' as object; added normalization rule to coerce to string

2026-02-24: Implemented initial streaming re-emitter; observed that naive chunking causes OA clients to interpret partial args as multiple invocation attempts — switched to buffering until function_call complete or 120ms timeout
2026-03-02: Snapshot schema landed in PR #1053; storage path uses existing artifacts S3 bucket with customer-scoped prefix. Need security sign-off for KMS key access for Private installs
2026-03-06: Added telemetry events for fallback decisions and mapping-errors; integrated with traces console (dashboard draft at /console/traces/oa-compat)
2026-03-08: QA running replay harness against 12 transcripts; 10 passed byte-compatibility, 2 failed due to whitespace tokenization differences — investigating tokenizer normalization strategies
references: RFC: streaming chunking semantics for OA-compat — rfc/2026-01-cc-streaming.md
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the snapshot field whitelist — sensitive data must not be persisted
Verify that functioncall buffering timeout (default 120ms) is conservative enough for low-latency apps but avoids partial-arg emission
Check telemetry naming and tag schema to ensure console dashboards can filter by customer and compat_version
